# Case study sources

The published case studies are claude.ai artifacts (links in the handovers). This folder keeps page sources (one folder per case study, each with a `README.md` entry; this index is generated by
`npm run docs`, never edited by hand) so a new
chat can reuse the Sitefloor bar, footer and patterns without re-reading a published page.

- `aldous-marr/index.html`: the jeweller case study (a stone under a loupe, read from table to culet: the hero is the
  Solitaire under a loupe you move yourself; Table is the home page, Crown Starter, Girdle Plus, Pavilion Signature,
  Culet the facts and speed; live engraving inside a band). Media (four clips, stills, worn photographs) live in the
  published artifact under `media/`.
- `calder-wyke/index.html`: the law firm case study (a deed between the firm and its website: an indenture-cut sheet,
  This Deed with its parties, Recitals (A)(B)(C), operative clauses 1–7 as the features with exhibits CW1–CW10 from the
  demo, a live probate estimator and a live if-there's-no-will; Schedules 1–3 are the plans; "time is of the essence"
  is the speed; executed under a blind CW stamp; a magpie palette, Literata and Geologica). Media (ten phone stills,
  780×1688) live in `media/` and the published artifact.
- `clemence/index.html`: the skin clinic case study (the proof: the page is a printer's proof of Clémence's treatment
  card, on cream proof paper with crop marks, a correction column in the margin and one red pencil. The hero is that
  pencil, live: write a line for a skin clinic's menu and the words the advertising rules catch (a named condition,
  "younger", "guaranteed", injectables, a result claimed for "it") are struck through as you type, numbered and
  explained in the margin with the CAP rule, using the same rules as the kit's `claimProblem`; beside it, the card
  Clémence's site prints instead, every line hers. The sheets that follow: the site in the card's own palm-and-gold
  frame with a phone laid over it; five words (the finder, live, with the demo's own cards and booking message); the
  card's three lines as a three-row proof (afterwards: the category pages; patch test: the patch-day tool, live; this
  evening: the rhythm reminders, live, from the demo's light-peel rhythm); one palm-green sheet for the Signature
  pieces (ritual and gift clips, the rituals page on a laptop); the plans as three printed cards; the numbers as a
  colophon; the close signed off with a "passed for press" stamp. Proof cream, ink, palm green, one gold rule, proof
  red for corrections only; Antic Didone and Baskervville (the demo's own), self-hosted with size-matched stand-ins,
  roman only). Media (three phone clips with posters, three phone stills, two laptop screens, three of the demo's
  photographs, the fonts) live in `media/` and the published artifact. Phone clips: CDP screencast at 390×844 and 2x
  in Chromium with `--lang=en-GB`, H.264; stills without the demo bar; nothing plays until asked.
- `corbel/index.html`: the electrician case study (the lighting plan of a website: the page opens dark on Corbel's
  house at dusk with one rotary dimmer, and the dial lights the photograph and every light drawn further down; a
  reflected ceiling plan where each room is a page of the site and each light, L01 to L17, a feature, its symbol the
  plan it comes on (downlight Starter, luminaire Plus, pendant Signature); the chapters are the schedule of fittings;
  a live fault guide and a live whole-house estimate from the demo's figures; the plans are three positions on the
  dial, Low, Evening, Full; the speed is "from the switch to the light"; drafting film with Corbel's blue as the ink
  and the light the one warm colour; Encode Sans Expanded and Encode Sans). Media (two phone clips, the house in 3D
  and the charger in 3D as 960×540 clips, posters, five phone stills, the demo's hero and garden-room photographs)
  live in the published artifact under `media/`. Phone clips: CDP screencast at 390×844 and 2x; 3D clips: one
  screenshot per frame with the page's animation clock stepped by hand, so the software renderer can't make them choppy.
- `datum-hire/index.html`: the car hire case study (directions to your door: the site read as the night drive that brings
  the car, a sat-nav instruction as the hero, one amber route line with each feature a stop at its mile marker, the plans
  as three motorway junctions on blue road-sign plates, the speed as the journey time, a live Delivered tonight with the
  demo's figures; night navy, Overpass and Overpass Mono). Media (four clips, posters, stills, four car photos) live in
  the published artifact under `media/`. Clips: Playwright at 390×844, scaled to 780 wide.
- `elsden/index.html`: the car storage case study (Hall One at eye level, from just inside the gate, in the dark. On
  arrival the strip lights strike one run at a time down the hall; pick a car and the floor outline of the free bay
  that fits glows, with a tag on the bay, using the same fit rule as the kit's `pickBay`. Every light was rendered on
  its own (Blender light groups); the page sums those passes in WebGL with a weight per light and tone-maps once, so
  each state is the render with those lights on. Without WebGL, or with reduced motion, it shows the lit stills. Then the hall drawn to scale
  from the demo's measurements wiped into the hall rendered from above, bay for bay; the live list (a Google Sheet you
  can change, with bays coming back, beside the free-bays line it feeds, and what the site says when the sheet goes quiet); the hall at night
  from above; the plans; the numbers. Plaster, ink, night navy, one warm light; Cardo and Radio Canada (Elsden's own),
  self-hosted with size-matched stand-ins). Media (the eye-level stills and light passes, the day and night aerials, a phone crop
  of the night aerial) live in the published artifact under `media/`; the fonts in `media/fonts/`. Nothing moves until
  asked; reduced motion skips the crossfade.
- `fendle/index.html`: the street-food stall case study (pull one: the page reads Fendle's website the way a bubble
  waffle is eaten, one bubble at a time. The hero is a real waffle in the open iron, full bleed, with fifteen of its
  bubbles as the kit's fifteen features; tap one and it lifts out of the photograph (the same pixels, clipped, with a
  shadow), leaves its empty cup behind, and a white card answers with the customer's question and the site's answer,
  live where the demo is (the next stop and its countdown on London time from Fendle's usual week, the party diary's
  Saturdays); a strip of the fifteen sits under the photograph for keyboards and phones. The chapters are six bubbles on
  raspberry, each a giant photographed bubble behind the demo on a phone: where we are, the board, parties, the drop,
  allergens, where to find us. The plans are Plain, Sauced and Loaded, three real waffles; the speed is "off the iron";
  the close asks for the stall's week. Iron black, raspberry, crust amber, batter cream; Gabarito and Labrada, the
  demo's own, self-hosted with size-matched stand-ins). Media (the iron photograph in two crops, six bubble crops, three
  plan photographs, eight phone stills, a laptop screen, the saved board picture, the fonts) live in `media/` and the
  published artifact. Phone stills: 390×844 at 2x in full Chrome, en-GB, London time, Saturday 21 November 2026, 15:00.
  Photographs (Pexels, free licence): the waffle iron, Th2city Santana,
  https://www.pexels.com/photo/waffle-on-iron-25757603/ (hero, bubbles, Plain); chocolate bubble waffles, Elizabeth
  Ferreira, https://www.pexels.com/photo/delicious-chocolate-bubble-waffles-in-food-truck-30461190/ (Sauced, cropped
  above the cones' print); bubble waffles with berries and nuts, Willians Huerta,
  https://www.pexels.com/photo/bubble-waffles-with-mixed-berries-and-nuts-34926596/ (Loaded).
- `fennick-lowe/index.html`: the tailor case study (cut to pattern: the page opens on Fennick & Lowe's charcoal flannel
  with a coat's manila pattern pieces laid on it, each piece a page of the site; tap one and a chalk line goes round it
  while that page shows on a phone lying on the cutting table; the pattern ticket lists every piece and the plan it
  comes on; chapters per piece (the cloth book and swatch set, the commission by code, the wedding party planner, from
  your pattern) with phone clips, and the specification card live on the page from the demo's own photographs; the
  plans are garments by their pieces, trousers (two), a jacket (five), the three-piece (up to twenty), each drawn as a
  cutter's marker; the speed is "measured twice", under a tape; Della Respira and Commissioner). Media (four phone
  clips with posters, nine phone stills, the cloth and the coat-on-stand photographs, specification and cloth tiles)
  live in the published artifact under `media/`. Phone clips: CDP screencast at 390×844 and 2x, encoded H.264.
- `grenat/index.html`: the grand café case study (a three-tier stand: Starter, Plus, Signature as savouries, scones and
  pâtisserie). Media (two phone clips, stills from the demo) live only in the published artifact.
- `halde/index.html`: the gym case study (the hour: a gym is a different place at 6am and at 6pm, and so is its
  website. The page opens on the demo's own hero, the club's count so large it crosses the photograph's edge and turns
  to negative over it, set by a rail of the day's twenty-four hours: each hour a fine rule as tall as the club's usual
  count, a day switch above it, and beneath it what the site shows a member at that hour (the doors, the next class,
  the next sauna slot, later today or first tomorrow), all from the demo's own figures and timetable. Pick a shut hour
  and the photograph dims slowly, the lights off. Chapters each open on one of the club's numbers: 15 minutes (the live
  count's age limit, with a slider for the sheet's age and a "can't be read" switch), £1,578 (the whole price under
  the DMCC Act, with a calculator using the kit's own rule), 6 classes (the class finder, film, and the timetable on a
  laptop), 21 weeks (the race planner, film), 85° (heat and cold, the only colour: the steam band with the figure
  crossing its foot, the cedar room), 5 rooms (film), 20 pages (a sideways strip of phones). The plans are priced the
  way Halde prices memberships, the first year's total first; the numbers are four measurements; the close is "your
  club, by the hour". Halde's black, bone and river stone; Epilogue (the demo's own), self-hosted with size-matched
  stand-ins). Media (three phone films with posters, fifteen phone stills, the timetable on a laptop, six of the
  demo's photographs, the fonts) live in `media/` and the published artifact. Phone films: CDP screencast at 390×844
  and 2x in Chromium with `--lang=en-GB`, H.264; stills and films without the demo ribbon; nothing plays until asked.
- `halvern/index.html`: the letting agent case study (going up: the page is a ride in the lift of a red-brick mansion
  block, from the street door to the roof, and every floor is a page of Halvern's website; the hero is the lift car,
  mahogany panels and a brass Art Deco floor indicator whose needle swings to the floor you press on the brass call
  panel, then the doors open on that floor; each floor opens with its number cast in brass, very large: G the home page
  and its lift plate, 1 Fees with the before-the-keys sums live from the demo's rules, 2 Residences and its filters,
  3 Areas and the journal, 4 For owners (the valuation sentence, onboarding, owner stories), 5 Moving in with the
  planner live (its calendar file saved from the demo page), R the building in 3D; a small brass plate keeps the floor you're on; the plans
  are three key fobs by the floors each key reaches; the speed is how long the doors take to open; mahogany and ivory,
  brass, one lamp-lit amber; Petrona, the demo's own). Media (four phone clips at 780×1688 and the building in 3D at
  1200 wide, posters, five phone stills, the porch and St John's Wood photographs, fonts) live in `media/` and the
  published artifact. Phone clips: Playwright with CDP screenshots at 390×844 and 2x, stitched at their real timing
  with ffmpeg; 3D clip: one screenshot per frame with the page's clock stepped by hand. Clip posters load only as a
  clip comes near, so the first screen's fonts arrive first.
- `hatheli/index.html`: the mehndi artist case study (dated to your wedding: the hero is one sentence, "My wedding is on
  Saturday 12 June 2027", its day, month and year set huge as the fields themselves, answered live from the demo's
  diary with the mehndi evening, the darkest day and the days left; every chapter below is a day of the bride's week
  counted back from that date, its number very large, Today, the trial, the outfit, the mehndi evening, paste off,
  the wedding, each re-dated when she changes hers; the ground follows the stain, bone for the bare palm, paste black
  for the mehndi night, the first orange for paste off, the darkest brown for the wedding; a live guest sum and a live
  "send to the family" message from the demo's own figures; "Your stain, day by day" described as Signature, from each
  artist's own photographs; the plans are three shades of one stain, Paste off, Overnight, On the day; the speed is
  "open before her hands are dry"; the demo's own Rozha One and Source Serif 4). Media (five phone clips with posters,
  four phone stills, the demo's window and chooda photographs) live in the published artifact under `media/`. Clips:
  Playwright screenshots at 390×844 and 2x, the demo ribbon hidden, stitched with ffmpeg at 10 fps.
- `isolde/index.html`: the bridal hair and makeup case study (one issue of her magazine: the page opens on the issue's
  cover held like the real thing, Isolde's name as the masthead with the bride's hair passing in front of it, the
  cover lines her live answers from the demo's own diary and prices (her date and "Open.", the price for the service
  she picks, "We start at 7:25am" for her ceremony), the cover price in the barcode corner the Starter plan; choose a
  wedding and the cover reprints, every folio re-dates to "The 25 September 2027 issue", the countdown re-counts; the
  contents page; This season as fashion pages; For the bride as the shopping page, prices with minutes in the chair;
  one dark spread, The morning, minute by minute, worked back live with the party steppers, two chairs and "This one
  needs planning — message me." exactly as the site does; Counted down (days left, the trial window, the skin steps
  dated, travel by postcode); the back of the book (guide pages and the journal); the plans as three subscriptions,
  The cover, The issue, The special edition; the speed as "On the stand in 1.4 seconds"; the back cover puts the
  reader's own business name on the masthead as they type it; the demo's own Libre Bodoni and Faustina). Its live
  parts run the demo's own logic and simulated diary, bundled into the page, so every answer matches Isolde's site.
  Media (two phone clips with posters, five phone stills, the demo's cover and cut-out, four looks and two
  photographs) live in `media/` and the published artifact. Clips: Playwright screenshots at 390×844 and 2x, the demo
  ribbon hidden, stitched with ffmpeg at 15 fps.
- `isotach/index.html`: the clothing-brand case study (a wind chart: lines of moving air bend around the phone; each
  feature is a numbered station; plans are wind barbs, Starter one feather, Plus two, Signature the pennant; no phone

- `laleh/index.html`: the social-first florist case study (her Instagram DMs: the page is one conversation, each
  chapter a customer's message set huge in italic on the left, often with the post they shared, and the reply from
  the right as Laleh's website answering it on a phone; the hero thread arrives once on load; live replies to "can
  you make this one?" (the real link check), "can u deliver today" (Laleh's cut-offs on London time) and "when's the
  next drop" (a countdown to Friday 7pm); the plans are pinned posts, one pin Starter, two Plus, three Signature;
  the speed is the message's "Delivered"; paper white with one peony, the messages the only round shapes; Tenor Sans
  and Spectral). Media (seven phone clips with posters, three phone stills, four demo photographs) live in the
  published artifact under `media/`. Clips: CDP screencast at 390×844 and 2x in full Chromium with `--lang=en-GB`
  (the headless shell ignores it, so date fields come out in US order), stitched with ffmpeg.
- `larchmere/index.html`: the wedding film case study (read by the sun's height: the page opens on Larchmere's film
  edge to edge with a live headline worked out from the sun's real elevation over Bibury now ("In Bibury the sun is
  8° up. Golden hour begins today at 15:34", "It's golden hour in Bibury now…"), and a degree scale down the left edge
  as the index with a glowing sun at its current height; each chapter sits at a height, +40° the film, +20° your date,
  +6° golden hour (with a live golden-hour field for any date), 0° the day, −4° your film, and its ground darkens from
  ivory to night; the plans at −6° are three lights, Daylight (Starter), Golden hour (Plus), Blue hour (Signature),
  each topped with a cut of that sky; the speed is "a degree every four minutes"; the demo's own fonts, Sorts Mill
  Goudy and Urbanist). The sun is NOAA's calculation, as in the kit's `lib/sun.js`. Media (the demo's wide and tall
  film with posters, three phone clips with posters, two phone stills) live in the published artifact under `media/`.
  Phone clips: Playwright screenshots at 390×844 and 2x in full Chromium with `--lang=en-GB` (UK date fields), one per
  step and one per typed letter, stitched with ffmpeg (the CDP screencast came out at 1x).
- `larrow/index.html`: the tour operator case study (twelve gores make a globe: the page opens on a globe-maker's
  gore sheet, the world cut into twelve 30° gores in Larrow's logbook ink, with each gore holding one month. Tap a
  month and its gore lights, the journey Larrow would send you on that month is drawn across it as a route with its
  stops, and an inset gives the photograph, nights, the place's local time (live) and its typical high from the
  demo's published climate figures; the page opens on this month in London. Chapters follow the gores: the logbook on
  a laptop (film), the year on a phone (film), local time (three live clocks), journeys and ATOL as given, when to go
  on a laptop, daylight, the shortlist and who's been there, the trip builder (film), travel-ready and the private
  trip page (film). The plans are three globes, Pocket, Table and Library; the numbers are "drawn to scale"; the close
  is "your year, on twelve gores". Ivory ground, logbook ink, one burnt-sienna accent taken from the demo; land from
  Natural Earth (public domain) projected as interrupted sinusoidal gores; Familjen Grotesk (the demo's own),
  self-hosted with a size-matched stand-in). Media (four films with posters, six phone stills, the when-to-go table on
  a laptop, five of the demo's photographs (one in two crops), the fonts) live in `media/` and the published artifact. Sideways strips are keyboard-reachable regions and each film button names its film. Phone films: CDP
  screencast at 390×844 and 2x in Chromium with `--lang=en-GB`, H.264; stills and films without the demo ribbon;
  nothing plays until asked.
- `linnet/index.html`: the cleaning case study (one visit, timed: the page is a fortnightly clean of a two-bedroom home
  with two bathrooms, 2 h 25 from 09:00. The hero is Linnet's room strip, live, under a headline that is the visit's
  length in words ("Two hours, twenty-five minutes."), so changing bedrooms, bathrooms or how often rewrites the
  headline, the price, the bill and the WhatsApp line together; "Play the visit" runs the clock from 09:00, filling each
  room as it's finished. Each room is a chapter opened by a time-sheet line (its minutes, huge, and where it sits in the
  visit): Kitchen and living is the price, Hall and stairs the questions before the door opens, the bedrooms a page for
  every clean, the bathrooms the work nobody sees; each chapter's task list is the features, marked by plan. The plans
  are three visit sheets added up like Linnet's bill; the speed is the time on site; the close is the finishing time.
  White with steel panels, ink, one kingfisher blue; Anek Latin, self-hosted, with size-matched fallbacks). Media
  (three phone clips with posters, four phone stills, two laptop screens, the demo's sitting-room and marble-bathroom
  photographs, the fonts) live in `media/` and the published artifact. Phone clips: CDP screencast at 390×844 and 2x in
  full Chromium with `--lang=en-GB`, encoded H.264; nothing plays until asked.
- `lyall-harrow/index.html`: the private wealth case study (a website read across fifty years: the page opens on the
  demo's misty shore with the site's own first question, "I am … and I live in …", set large over the photograph and
  answering as the site does; the page is indexed by horizon on one copper hairline, Today 2026, This year 2027, Ten

  meeting field that refuses account numbers; the showpiece is the firm's insights sheet, editable on the one navy
  band, publishing to the page only when compliance ticks, names and dates a row and holding back any promise of a
  return; a live What to gather per moment, to tick and print; the plans are three horizons, Today, This decade,
  Generations; white with one navy band, copper hairlines, Mona Sans at 125% width for display). Media (six phone
  stills at 780×1688 and five of the demo's photographs) live in `media/` and the published artifact.
- `marese/index.html`: the lingerie case study (a stocking's back seam: one stitched line down the page, each feature a

  one black; a live hint composer and a countdown to Marese's Valentine's order-by). Media (six phone clips with posters,

- `marlie/index.html`: the teeth whitening case study (the social six: the page opens on a cosmetic dentist's planning
  screen, a real smile in black and white with the guides drawing themselves on it, the midline, the commissure line
  at its measured 2.6°, the smile arc along the edges, and the six front teeth 13 12 11 | 21 22 23 marked with their
  widths against the front tooth; touch a tooth and the readout names it and its chapter. The midline then runs down
  the whole page and each chapter is one of the six, numbered as a dentist numbers it (FDI), opening on the six with
  its own tooth marked and sitting on its own side of the line: 11 the booth strip, 21 tell me what you'd change
  (live, with the demo's words), 12 nothing it can't keep (GDC lines and a live claims check that refuses shade,
  permanence, guarantee, laser and specialist promises as the kit does), 22 when's the big day (live, the demo's
  timings), 13 visit by visit and aftercare, 23 smiles with consent and arriving; the premolars list the rest of the
  site; the plans are the golden proportion, Signature 1.618, Plus 1, Starter 0.618, drawn at those widths; the speed
  is read off a rule in tenths of a second; the demo's own fonts, Reddit Sans and Brygada 1918 italic, with Reddit Mono
  for every measurement). Media (the smile photograph, three phone clips with posters, six phone stills) live in
  `media/` and the published artifact. Phone captures: full Chromium at 390×844 and 2x with `--lang=en-GB`, the demo
  ribbon hidden; the strip clip recorded with CSS animations at a quarter speed (CDP `Animation.setPlaybackRate`)
  and played back at full speed, so it's smooth.

  Photograph credits: `media/smile.webp` (the hero, every chapter's crop and the closing figure) is "Close Up Photo of
  Person's Lips" by Amir SeilSepour, a model photograph, free under the Pexels licence:
  https://www.pexels.com/photo/close-up-photo-of-person-s-lips-11956948/. Every other image and clip is a capture of
  the smile demo, whose photographs are credited in `sites/demos/smile/img/CREDITS.md`.
- `marrick/index.html`: the personal trainer case study (while you train: the page opens on the trainer's week as one
  appointment book, Monday to Sunday, 06:00 to the night, the sessions ruled in ink and, in walnut, eight entries I to

- `maudry/index.html`: the event designer case study (the table plan: the site read as one evening in the room Maudry
  dressed. The page opens at the door on the table plan, a cream card on a brass easel under its own picture light,
  with the room laid for dinner beyond (a render, one camera, the card square to it). The plan's guests are the people
  who come to the site (the couple a year out, the events lead, the venue manager, the couple choosing flowers, the

  visual"); 20:15 dinner for 120 (the room drawn live for a number, a room and a layout, in the kit's own words, with
  "A guide: the venue's own capacity and rules decide."); 21:30 the brief (live: only what was chosen, as Maudry
  receives it, and the key dates worked back from the day); 22:30 the proposal by code; 23:15 the tables (the plans as
  a table for two, a table for five and a table for twenty, a seat for each page); midnight, carriages (the numbers).
  Live pieces use the kit's rules and wording (`nextFree`, `dateWords`, `briefMessage`, `keyDates`, `drawRoom`,
  `roomWords`) and the demo's own rooms, key dates and diary rule. Maudry's warm dark, parchment and olive, brass as
  hairlines, the card's cream the one light ground; Eczar (the demo's own), self-hosted with the look's size-matched
  stand-ins per weight. Media (the table plan render at three sizes, the three design visuals and three dressings,
  twelve phone stills, the home page on a laptop, the fonts) live in `media/` and the published artifact. Phone stills:
  390×844 at 2x in Chromium with `--lang=en-GB`, London time, 26 November 2026, without the demo ribbon. Motion: slow
  fades, only when asked; none under reduced motion.

  (hold a light to plain paper and the regulator's status line appears; the demo's footer on a phone), III serial

  holographic foil, the same rules as the kit's `milestones`, plus a film), VI the thread (old pensions, a security

  us). The plans are three denominations, each note larger than the last; the numbers are "cleared"; the close is

Every case study must look unrecognisably different from the others, keep the same Sitefloor bar and footer, and never
show how we built anything (CLAUDE.md rule 11a).
